newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernomyrdin not planning meet Belarus leader-aide.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin not planning meet Belarus leader-aide.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin has no plans to meet Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko to discuss his battle with parliament, a Russian government spokesman said on Wednesday.
Lukashenko aide Ural Latypov said in Minsk that Chernomyrdin might go to Belarus to meet Lukashenko on Friday or Saturday.
But Igor Shabdurasulov, head of the Russian government's culture and information department, later said Chernomyrdin was planning a trip to Murmansk in northern Russia on Friday.
"We have no other information about the premier's working plans on this score," Itar-Tass news agency quoted him as saying.

Lukashenko had earlier snubbed an invitation to attend a meeting with his main political opponent, parliamentary speaker Semyon Sharetsky, and parliamentary leaders from Russia in the Russian city of Smolensk on Wednesday.
The meeting had been scheduled by Russia to solve the political crisis in Belarus, where parliament is trying to stop Lukashenko extending his powers in a referendum on Sunday.
Lukashenko's closest aide, Vladimir Zametalin, told Reuters that the president did not go to Smolensk because Chernomyrdin would not be there.
Latypov said Lukashenko would visit the town of Brest on the Polish border about 350 km (200 miles) west of Minsk on Thursday to continue his referendum campaign.
